title: Developer experience: SDK guides, quickstarts & API examples — operating procedures and canonical fixes
author: Ava Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page defines the operating procedures, canonical templates, and the top support issues & fixes for all Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and docs-site operations. The goal is to keep on‑ramp materials low‑friction, accurate, and fast to iterate when support signals regressions.

Scope
- SDK guides (Python, Node, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and templates for sample apps and reference integrations
- API examples (generation, streaming, function/tool-calling, embeddings)
- Docs site operations (edit, review, publish, rollback)
- Top support issues -> canonical fixes and ownership

Principles (apply to all DevEx pages)
1. Single-source of truth: examples on the docs site must be runnable and pinned to a commit/SDK version.
2. Minimal friction: quickstarts should be runnable in <= 5 minutes with clear environment steps.
3. Observable and testable: include CI smoke tests that run examples and gated checks on docs changes.
4. Ownership and SLAs: every page must have an owner_team and an author; documented issues have a triage owner and SLA.

Standard page types and required sections
- SDK Guide 
  - Short overview and when to use this SDK (bullet list)
  - Install (pin exact version)
  - Auth/Config example (env var names)
  - Quick snippet (sync and streaming if supported)
  - Error handling and common pitfalls
  - API compatibility / migration notes
  - Test matrix (supported runtime versions)

- Quickstart Template (single repo)
  - Prereqs (account, API key, node/python version)
  - 5-minute setup steps (numbered)
  - Run & expected output
  - Where to extend for production

- API Example page
  - Example request (JSON) and response (JSON)
  - Latency/cost notes for the pattern
  - When to prefer streaming vs non-streaming

Canonical Quickstarts (recommended templates)
- template-minimal-node: minimal Node.js app showing generation + streaming (recommended: node 18, SDK @redwood/inference v1.4.0)
- template-minimal-python: minimal Python app showing generation + embeddings (recommended: python 3.10, redwood-sdk==1.4.0)
- template-embed-search: embedding + vector search quickstart (simple Flask/Express microservice)
- template-tooling: function/tool calling example (client + simple tool runner)

Example quickstart (Node)
1) Prereqs:
   - Node 18+
   - REDWOOD_API_KEY in environment
2) Install:
   npm init -y
   npm install @redwood/inference@1.4.0
3) Example snippet (save as index.mjs):

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
async function main(){
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/base-lite', input: 'Summarize: Redwood helps teams run LLM inference' });
  console.log(r.output);
}
main().catch(console.error);
```

Expected output: single-string summary. If you receive an auth error check REDWOOD_API_KEY or ensure API key has "developer" scope.

Example quickstart (Python)
1) Prereqs: Python 3.10, virtualenv
2) Install:
   python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
   pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0
3) snippet (app.py):

```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model='redwood/base-lite', input='Write a friendly hello message')
print(resp.output)
```

Docs site operating procedures (publish flow)
1. Make changes in the docs repo branch (docs/<area>/YYYYMMDD-short-desc).
2. Add smoke tests: any change to an example must add/update a smoke test in ci/docs-smoke-tests. CI will run quickstarts in a sandbox using a test key.
3. Add or update the page metadata header (title, author, owner_team, reviewers, labels, created_at, last_updated).
4. Open PR with description and link to smoke test run. Mark as in_review.
5. Reviewer checklist (required):
   - Code examples run locally and in CI
   - No hard-coded secrets or customer IDs
   - Changes to API examples cross-checked with backend API contract (attach contract id)
   - Update related_pages links and labels
6. Merge -> incremental deploy to staging docs site -> staged review by reviewer -> promote to production.

Rollback procedure (for broken examples or regressions)
1. Revert PR that introduced the change, open a fast follow PR with corrected example.
2. If rollback required urgently during business hours, page owner triggers a hotfix branch and tag for immediate deploy.
3. Notify #devex and #sre with summary and mitigation steps.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (most frequent)
Note: owners listed are the primary triage contact; escalate to eng-developer-experience if owner unavailable.

| Issue (symptom) | Likely root cause | Canonical fix | Owner | Docs page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SDK import error / build fails | SDK version mismatch or breaking change | Pin SDK version in quickstart, add migration note; update CI test matrix | Jamal Ortiz | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-quickstart-template |
| Auth error (401) when running examples | Missing/misconfigured REDWOOD_API_KEY or wrong scope | Update quickstart to document required scopes; include troubleshooting snippet to print env; add smoke test to assert 200 | Priya Nair | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/auth-troubleshooting |
| Streaming examples drop connection mid-stream | Example uses short socket timeout or incorrect streaming boundary handling | Add retry/backpressure guidance; show client-side reconnect pattern; advise SRE to check proxy timeouts (nginx/gateway) | eng-platform | /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/streaming-timeouts |
| Example output differs from docs | Example pinned to floating model or new model default | Pin model versions in examples and add note "pinned to model X at commit Y"; schedule periodic re-eval | applied-ml-and-evals | /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks |
| Embedding similarity low in sample | Pre/post-processing mismatch or embedding model drift | Document standard normalization steps in quickstart; add test that asserts similarity > threshold for control queries | eng-developer-experience | /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/embedding-quickstart |

Canonical triage runbook (for support-facing doc regressions)
1. Reproduce: run example in staging using the docs smoke test harness. Capture logs and error messages.
2. Identify scope: SDK-only, API contract, backend behavior, or infra (timeouts, proxy).
3. Apply quick fix if low-risk (typo, pin version, missing env var).
4. If backend change required, open internal issue and link ticket number in PR.
5. Communicate: update the original support case with summary and ETA, update #devex and the page's related_pages with the issue id.

Content templates (short)
- SDK Guide header template (top lines to copy)
  Title: <SDK name> guide
  Summary: 1–2 line summary
  Prereqs: runtime, SDK version, env vars
  Quick example: code block + expected output
  Troubleshooting: top 3 errors and fixes
  Test matrix: linux/mac/osx, versions
  Owner: team/name

- Quickstart checklist (pre-merge)
  - Example runs locally in 5 minutes
  - CI smoke-test added or updated
  - Version pins present for SDK/model/deps
  - Reviewer approved and labels added

Metrics and SLAs
- Doc issue response SLA: acknowledge support-driven doc issues within 24 hours; triage and schedule a fix within 5 business days.
- Example regressions causing production impact: target fix in 48 hours (owner_team escalation to eng-platform/eng-sre as needed).
- Coverage goal: 100% of quickstarts must have a CI smoke test.

Ownership and contact points
- Default owner_team for quickstarts & sdk guides: eng-developer-experience.
- Triage rotation: weekly on-call list in #devex-triage.
- Escalation: ping eng-platform (for infra), applied-ml-and-evals (for model behavior), eng-sre (for latency/timeouts).

Change log
- 2025-06-15: initial draft (Ava Chen)
- 2025-10-02: added streaming rollback guidance (reviewer: Jamal Ortiz)
- 2026-02-10: updated canonical fixes table and tightened CI smoke-test requirement (reviewer: Priya Nair)

Appendix: Useful CI commands and smoke test snippets
- Run Node quickstart smoke test:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=testkey node ci/smoke-tests/node/quickstart-test.mjs
- Run Python quickstart smoke test:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=testkey python ci/smoke-tests/python/quickstart_test.py

If you make a docs change that affects an example output, add a short note at the top of the page with the model version and commit SHA used to generate the sample output. This ensures reproducibility and makes triage faster when support cases reference example outputs.
